title: Product of All the Others

concept.title: Prefix and suffix products
body: For each position you want the product of all elements except the one at that position. Dividing the total by `a[i]` is not allowed (it fails for zeros, and under a modulo it needs an inverse). Instead notice that the product of the others is **(product of everything to the left) times (product of everything to the right)**.

body.code:
left[i] = a[0] * ... * a[i - 1]      # computed left to right
right   = a[i + 1] * ... * a[n - 1]  # kept in a running variable, right to left
result[i] = left[i] * right

body: Two passes give all results in O(n). Because the products get huge, they are asked modulo 1000000007 (take every number modulo 1000000007 first, making negative numbers non-negative).

statement: Given an array of `n` integers, print for every position `i` the product of all elements except `a[i]`, **modulo 1000000007**. The printed results must be in the range 0 to 1000000006 (a negative product is made positive by adding multiples of the modulus).

examples.note: The products are 6, -3 and -2; modulo 1000000007 the last two are 1000000004 and 1000000005.

hints: Compute for every i the product of the elements to its left.
Go from the right with a running product of the elements to the right of i.
Take every number modulo 1000000007 first, and the product modulo after each multiplication.

explanation: The product of the others is the product on the left times the product on the right. One pass stores the left products, a second pass from the right multiplies in the right products.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

MOD = 10**9 + 7
vals = [x % MOD for x in a]
left = [1] * n
for i in range(1, n):
    left[i] = left[i - 1] * vals[i - 1] % MOD
right = 1
res = [0] * n
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    res[i] = left[i] * right % MOD
    right = right * vals[i] % MOD
print(*res)
